title: I spent 9.4 billion tokens building a racing game with AI agents: 44 days, 403 commits, 26 circuits - Still Building!!!
author: Senior_Refuse5031
selftext:
Built this solo by directing AI coding agents. Here's how it actually went:

**How it was made**

* October on Codex (GPT-6), November on Claude Code. One model reviews the designs; others write the code.
* 38 sessions, 288 sub-agents, 460 messages from me. I direct and playtest; the agents build.
* 98% of the 9.4B tokens were agents re-reading their own context. Only about 26M were actual output.
* What it cost: about $535 in AI subscriptions over 3 months.

**What the agents built**  
APEX Formula Club, a low-poly open-wheel racer that runs in the browser. It has 26 circuits, qualifying, pit stops, car damage, weather and a full championship, and the whole game is under 50 MB.

**What they got wrong**  
Cars tunnelling through walls, circuits drifting off-scale, and runaway jobs that once filled my disk. Most of the work was reviewing and testing, not prompting.

Still building. The full game launches 12 Dec. Happy to answer anything about the workflow.
